hook: You bill $74.65 an hour. You keep $52.08
hook_say: Here is where one billed hour really goes on a $60,000 take-home. The free hourly rate calculator runs the same maths on your numbers.

rows.label: Take-home pay you want per year
rows.why: The calculator's example: a $60,000 take-home goal.

rows.label: Tax set-aside, business expenses
rows.say: Set aside 25 percent for tax, plus $6,000 of costs
rows.why: 25% set aside for tax and $6,000 of yearly business costs: $86,000 of revenue needed.

rows.label: Hours a client pays for
rows.say: Clients pay for 60 percent of your hours
rows.why: 48 weeks of 40 hours is 1,920 hours worked. At 60% billable, clients pay for 1,152 of them.

rows.label: Minimum hourly rate
rows.why: $86,000 over 1,152 billable hours: $74.65 an hour, $75 on a rate card.

rows.label: Of each billable hour, you keep
rows.why: Each billable hour splits into $52.08 take-home, $17.36 tax set-aside and $5.21 of expenses.

fix.label: Bill 80% of your hours: rate needed
fix.say: Bill 80 percent of your hours and you need $55.99
fix.why: Same goal, tax and costs: at 80% billable the rate you need drops to $55.99 an hour.
